title: Three Reasons to Be Glad to Go to Church
speaker: Jonathan Baird
summary: God is there, the truth is there and his people are there. Don't let church become just another thing on the calendar.
exhortation: We're coming up on the weekend. Are you excited to go to church? Are you excited to be with the people of God? You should be. Here are three reasons to be excited to go to church this weekend.

Reason number one: God is there. Psalm 27:4 says, "One thing have I asked of the Lord, that will I seek after: that I may dwell in the house of the Lord all the days of my life, to gaze upon the beauty of the Lord and to inquire in his temple." David understood that God was uniquely present in his house. As we go to church this weekend, remember promises like "where two or three are gathered in my name, there am I among them." We say that so often, but what a powerful promise for God to make: that he will be present with us when we gather together.

Reason number two: the truth is there. We go through our week in a world that hates the truth, in a culture that speaks lies, and the church brings the truth like a drink of cold water when you're thirsty. If you have time, read through Psalm 73 and meditate on it. It shows a man caught up in the culture of the world. He's looking at wealthy, wicked people and seeing them thrive and win, and it's getting him down and even causing him to doubt God and his word. Then he says, "But when I thought how to understand this, it seemed to me a wearisome task, until I went into the sanctuary of God; then I discerned their end." We need to gather with the people of God and go to church to be reset with the truth: to understand that God is in control, that he is sovereign, and that the wicked will not win. Righteousness will win out. Not our righteousness, but the righteousness of God in Christ.

And finally, we go to church because the people of God are there. Psalm 133 says, "Behold, how good and pleasant it is when brothers dwell in unity!" I saw a clip of a well-known podcaster talking about visiting a church in Austin. He said if there were a pill you could take to be like these people, he'd take it. They were the nicest, kindest people, and it was such a wonderful place to be. You could see him recognize that this was different, that these people treat each other differently. The kindness, the generosity, the passion. He was really affected by it. What a joy it is to go to church and fellowship with fellow believers. It's not like hanging out at work. It's a deeper fellowship.

Our lives get pretty busy, and sometimes church can start to feel like just another thing on the calendar. Don't treat it like that. Get excited this weekend to be with the people of God. And if you see someone who's downcast, pray for God to give you joy and fill you with the Holy Spirit, so you can reach out to others and lift them up this weekend.
prayer: How good it is to be with your people. Thank you for your church, Lord. Thank you for the body that is meant to work together: an eye, an ear, a hand, a foot. The body of Christ is intended to work together.

Lord, I pray we would fight against any discouragement in our hearts that says the church isn't what you intended or isn't operating the way it should. Even where that is true in certain places, I pray we would press into the wonderful truth of the body of Christ as you intended it: where we can encourage each other, grow with each other, and run the race together with other saints, to be encouraged, to be lifted up, to be filled with your Spirit, and to be equipped for mission. These things happen at church. So I pray that our hearts would be freshly excited and encouraged to be with your people and in your house. In Jesus' name, amen.
